transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you. Um, well, I'm mainly here because my sleep has just gotten so incredibly unreliable lately. Like, I will go to bed completely exhausted, but I just lie there staring at the ceiling, replaying all my sales forecasts and team issues. 

Which, honestly, my team has been such a handful this month. I had to sit down with one of my senior reps, Dave, because he keeps bypassing the new CRM system, and it's messing up my entire pipeline report for corporate. I swear, corporate rolls out these new tech tools without actually training anyone, and then I'm the one who has to clean up the mess and play tech support. It's ridiculous, and the interface doesn't even make sense if you're actually out in the field. 

But... um, anyway, what was I saying? Right, so I'm just lying there thinking about all that, and even when I finally do drift off, I almost always end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning. And once I'm up, I just can't get my brain to power down again.
How long has this problem with your sleep been going on?

Um, well, it’s been building for a while now. I’d say it really started back when they did the big sales division reorganization, which was... gosh, about thirteen months ago now. 

God, that reorg was an absolute nightmare. They brought in this outside consulting firm—these guys in overly expensive suits who clearly had never sold a single thing in their lives—and they just decided to completely restructure all our territories. Suddenly I was covering the entire Midwest region, which meant I had to start flying out of O'Hare instead of Midway. And O'Hare is just the absolute worst. The TSA lines are always wrapped around the building, and the last time I was there, I had to pay like thirty dollars for a sad little wilted salad and a bottle of water. Plus, the parking... don't even get me started on the parking situation in Terminal 2. They've been doing construction there for what feels like a decade, and you have to take this shuttle that smells like wet dog just to get to the main concourse. 

But, um... wait, I'm sorry, what was the question? Oh, right, my sleep. Yeah, so, since the reorganization. About thirteen months.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about things other than work, like personal relationships, health, or everyday responsibilities?

Um, yeah, I mean, it's not just work, though work is a huge part of it. Most days my mind just... it just jumps around constantly. Like, I'll be worrying about whether we'll hit the launch numbers, and then suddenly I'm stressing over whether someone on my team is about to quit. And then from there, it's right into worrying about the mortgage, or this one client renewal that's coming up. 

Actually, speaking of the mortgage, my husband and I just tried to refinance because the rates dipped for like half a second, right? But the amount of paperwork they wanted was insane. They wanted tax returns from three years ago, and I had to dig through all these old boxes in the basement. And our basement is just a disaster zone right now because we had that heavy rain last month and a little bit of water seeped in near the water heater. We had to get this guy out to look at it, and he was completely useless. He just shined a flashlight around and charged us a hundred and fifty bucks for a "consultation fee." I swear, contractors these days just make up numbers. I should have just gone to Home Depot and bought some of that waterproof sealant myself, you know? They have it in aisle 14, right next to the caulking guns. 

But... um, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, worrying. Yeah, it just feels like every small delay or issue could turn into something major. Like my brain just spirals out of control with it all.
Do you find it hard to control or stop your worrying, even when you try to distract yourself or tell yourself it's not helpful?

Um, yeah, exactly. I really can't stop it. Like, I will literally sit there and tell myself, "Brenda, you've done the plan, you've done everything you can, just let it go." But it doesn't work. Like, five minutes later, I'm right back in another loop. It's like playing whack-a-mole—I check one concern off the list, and then three more just pop up out of nowhere. 

Speaking of lists, I actually use this really great app on my phone for lists now. It's called Todoist, I don't know if you've heard of it, but you can color-code everything and set priority levels. I have my work tasks in red and personal stuff in blue. Though, honestly, I spent like three hours last Sunday just organizing the lists instead of actually doing any of the things on them. My husband was making fun of me because I was sitting on the couch ignoring this documentary we were supposed to be watching together. It was about deep-sea creatures, which usually I love. Did you know there are these jellyfish that are biologically immortal? They can just revert back to their polyp stage when they get stressed out or injured. I mean, imagine if people could do that. Just hit a reset button when things get too overwhelming. I'd probably be a polyp right now. 

But... wait, sorry, what was the question? Oh, right, controlling the worry. Yeah, no, I try to distract myself, but it just doesn't work. I'm always back in the loop.
Do you notice any physical symptoms, like restlessness, feeling on edge, muscle tension, or fatigue, especially when you're worrying?

Um, yeah, actually. I feel wound up almost all the time. It's like... it's like I'm sitting in a pipeline review with the regional VP, even when I'm just at home eating dinner. And my shoulders, they stay so tight no matter how much I try to relax them. 

I actually tried getting a massage for it a couple of weeks ago. There's this place in the strip mall near my house, right next to that frozen yogurt place that always looks like it's going out of business but never actually does. The massage therapist's name was Sven, and he had these huge hands, like frying pans. He kept telling me to breathe into my back, which I still don't understand how you're supposed to do. Like, anatomically, that makes no sense. But anyway, they played this really weird music the whole time. It was supposed to be relaxing, I guess, but it sounded like a mix between whale sounds and wind chimes, and it just made me think about that documentary again, the one with the immortal jellyfish. Did you know some whales can live to be over two hundred years old? I read that they found one with a harpoon tip from the 1800s still stuck in it. Imagine carrying something around with you for that long. 

But... oh gosh, I'm doing it again, aren't I? What did you ask me? Oh, physical stuff. Yeah, the tightness in my shoulders and just feeling constantly on edge. It's pretty much all the time.
Do you ever feel anxious or on edge even when there isn’t anything specific going on at work or at home that should be causing it?

Um, yeah, I guess so. It's like, even if it's a Saturday morning and there's literally nothing on the schedule, I still have this... this feeling humming in the background. Like I'm waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? 

Speaking of shoes, I actually just bought a new pair of running shoes because I thought maybe jogging would help burn off some of this energy. They're those really bright neon green ones? I usually go for black or gray because they don't show the dirt as much, especially with the trails around here. The trails get so muddy after it rains, and the city never puts down enough gravel. There was this one time I was walking the trail with my friend Jessica—she just moved here from Denver, actually. She was telling me how the altitude there makes baking a cake a total nightmare. You have to adjust the flour and the baking powder, and even the oven temperature. I used to love baking, mostly cupcakes. I had this great recipe for red velvet with cream cheese frosting, but cream cheese has gotten so expensive lately. I was at the grocery store the other day, and a tiny little block of it was almost five dollars. Five dollars! And don't even get me started on the price of eggs. 

Wait, sorry. I'm rambling again, aren't I? What did you ask me about? Oh, feeling on edge for no reason. Yeah, even when everything is completely fine and quiet, I just... I can't seem to turn it off.
Have you noticed feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like baking or watching documentaries?

Um, feeling down? I don't... I don't think so. I mean, I still like documentaries and stuff. It's just hard to sit through them sometimes because I'm so jittery. 

But I haven't baked in a while, actually. It's not really that I lost interest, it's just... well, like I said, the grocery prices are insane. And honestly, baking takes so much precision. You have to measure everything exactly. If you mess up the baking soda, the whole thing tastes like soap. I did that once when I was trying to make my husband a birthday cake. It was supposed to be a surprise, so I was rushing while he was out picking up dry cleaning. Our dry cleaner is this really sweet older man who always gives out those strawberry candies with the wrappers that look like actual strawberries? I don't know where he buys them, I've literally never seen them in a store. Maybe he orders them in bulk online. I should look that up on Amazon. Amazon has everything now. I bought my running shoes there, actually, the neon green ones. Shipping was delayed, though, which was super annoying because I had all this momentum to start jogging, and then I had to wait three days. 

Sorry, wait. What were we talking about? Oh, right. Being depressed or something. No, I don't think I'm depressed. I still care about things, I just... I just have too much nervous energy to focus on them right now.
Do you ever feel down or sad for most of the day, even when things aren’t particularly stressful or worrying?

Um, sad for most of the day? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I don't wake up feeling like there's a raincloud over me or anything. It's more like a... like a buzzing feeling, you know? 

Speaking of buzzing, my phone has been vibrating non-stop this morning. I think it's because they finally updated the app we use for tracking our sales leads, and now every time someone even looks at an account, it sends a notification. It's so distracting. I actually had to put it in my desk drawer yesterday just so I could finish writing an email. My desk drawer is completely jammed right now, by the way. I have this habit of hoarding those little packets of soy sauce you get from sushi places. We have this great sushi place near the office, they do this spicy tuna roll with jalapeños on top. It sounds weird, but it's actually amazing. I took my sister there when she visited last month. She's a teacher, so she's always looking for a deal, and they have this incredible lunch special. She teaches third grade, which I could never do. Kids that age have so much energy, they just bounce off the walls. 

Wait, sorry. I completely lost my train of thought. What did you ask me? Oh, feeling sad. No, I don't really feel sad. Just... just really wired and anxious, I guess.
Have you ever had sudden episodes of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes, where you felt like something terrible was going to happen and you couldn’t escape?

Um, intense fear that peaks in minutes? No, I don't think I've ever had anything like that. I don't get sudden spikes where I feel like I'm trapped or anything. It's more of a constant, steady thing. 

Speaking of being trapped, though, I got stuck in the elevator at work last Tuesday. Just for a few minutes, but still. The maintenance guy said it was an issue with the sensor on the door. He was this really tall guy, must have been at least six-four, and he had this huge ring of keys that jingled every time he moved. It reminded me of the janitor at my elementary school. Mr. Henderson, I think his name was? He used to let us help him clap the chalk erasers outside. You know, back when schools actually used chalkboards instead of those smart boards. I don't even know how those smart boards work, honestly. My sister uses one in her classroom, and she says the kids are always messing with the calibration so when she tries to write, the line appears like two inches away from the pen. Technology is so frustrating sometimes. Like my laptop charger—it only works if you bend the cord at this very specific angle. I really need to buy a new one, but the official ones are so expensive, and the cheap knockoffs always overheat. I read this article about a cheap charger catching fire and burning a hole right through someone's mattress. 

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again. What was the question? Oh, the sudden panic things. No, I don't have those. Just the regular, all-the-time worrying.
Have you noticed any days where you feel unusually empty, hopeless, or where you’re not able to feel pleasure in things that usually bring you joy, even for a few hours at a time?

Um, feeling empty or hopeless? No, I don't really get that. I mean, I don't feel empty. If anything, my brain feels way too full, like it's just constantly running through a checklist that never ends. 

Speaking of checklists, I was trying to organize my grocery list by aisle yesterday because it's supposed to save time, right? But the grocery store completely rearranged their layout. They moved the cereal to where the baking supplies used to be, which makes zero sense. I spent like ten minutes just looking for oatmeal. I usually get the steel-cut kind because I read it's better for your cholesterol. My dad had high cholesterol, and he had to go on this super strict diet where he basically only ate unseasoned chicken and steamed broccoli for a year. He was so miserable. He used to sneak spoonfuls of peanut butter when my mom wasn't looking. They always bought that natural peanut butter where the oil separates at the top, and you have to stir it for like five minutes before you can even use it. I hate that stuff. It always gets all over my hands, and then I have to wash them three times just to get the grease off. The soap in my kitchen smells like lemon, which is nice, but it really dries out my skin. I should probably buy some hand lotion to keep by the sink. I saw this lavender one at the farmer's market last weekend... 

Sorry, I'm rambling again, aren't I? What did you ask? Oh, right, feeling hopeless or not enjoying things. No, I don't really have days like that. I still enjoy things, I just can't seem to relax enough to actually focus on them.
